correctness.rationale: Direct definitions on the 16 labeled vertices, a checkable 256-entry neighborhood incidence certificate, an analytic 80-set and 32-claw classification, plus two different exhaustive Python 3 verifiers each visiting all 65536 subsets of each graph. This fixed finite result needs no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Narrowed to the exact Shrikhande paired-domination polynomial, its 32 minimum unmatchable claws, and contrast against a known four-by-four rook paired polynomial. Searches for alternative names, equal-neighborhood-incidence formulations, graph domination polynomials, and exact 48/80 counts returned no equivalent covering theorem in the inspected literature or accessible earlier findings. Crucially, prior rook-polynomial and bipartite-incidence results are excluded from novelty. Full-text access limitations and unindexed literature are documented; novelty is a best-evidence rather than exhaustive historical certification.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande/rook pair is a canonical nonisomorphic pair of strongly regular graphs with the same local numerical parameters. A complete matchability-sensitive polynomial distinction despite the same total-domination polynomial is a natural, structurally explained separation: exactly 32 minimum Shrikhande total guards form claws not admitting a perfect matching. The full discrepancy polynomial gives a reusable benchmark for structure-sensitive domination on the smallest standard SRG comparison pair; neither computing code nor search absence alone supplies this value.
